prompt:
Use the supplied function definitions. If a function directly fits the requested action, return exactly one actual function call with a JSON object of arguments, using its supplied name. Otherwise make no call and reply briefly in plain text. General questions, writing help, small talk, and unsupported actions (device alarms, flight bookings, invoice payments) do not fit; topic mentions and timestamps do not make them fit.

For scheduling, a clock time for the item means create_event; a dated to-do without a clock time means create_task, even with scheduling language. A completed phone call means log_call; a future timed call means create_event. Other supported intents: look up a person's contact details, send email, search internal documents, get city weather, and convert currency. Use add_todo or query_knowledge_base instead of create_task or search_docs when those are the names supplied; apply the same rules in Swedish.

Fill all required fields from the request without inventing values or asking for information already given. Omit unprovided optional fields (documented defaults normal, 10, and celsius are tolerated). Leave weather date absent for now or unspecified dates; leave currency date absent if no rate date is given. Copy quoted titles, subjects, and search phrases verbatim without quotes or translation. Use the final correction; when a recipient has multiple addresses, choose the company-domain address over gmail.com, outlook.com, hotmail.com, or icloud.com regardless of order. Attendees is an array of only the other named people's full names.

Output numeric amounts and minute durations. Interpret English comma grouping and decimal points, and Swedish space grouping and decimal commas. Half an hour, one hour, one and a half hours, and two hours are 30, 60, 90, and 120 minutes. Urgent/high priority = high; low priority = low. Spoke with/talked to/reached = connected; left voicemail = voicemail; no answer/didn't pick up = no_answer. ISO codes: euros/€ EUR; US dollars/dollars/$ USD; pounds/£ GBP; Swedish kronor (including Swedish kronor/kr without a country qualifier) SEK; Norwegian kroner NOK; Danish kroner DKK; Swiss francs CHF; yen/¥ JPY.

Today is Tuesday 2026-11-17. Output YYYY-MM-DD and 24-hour HH:MM; interpret am/pm and Swedish clock notation (kl., klockan, dot-separated minutes). Weeks are Monday–Sunday: this week Nov 16–22, next Nov 23–29, last Nov 9–15. Tomorrow (i morgon/imorgon) +1; day after tomorrow (i övermorgon) +2; yesterday (i går/igår) −1; in N days (om N dagar) +N; N days ago (för N dagar sedan) −N. In one/two weeks (om en/två veckor, singular vecka for one) +7/+14; a week ago (för en vecka sedan) −7. On/this weekday (på + weekday) is the first occurrence strictly after today; next (nästa) weekday is in next week; last weekday (i + Swedish weekday with past -s form) is in last week. For a yearless date, use the next occurrence on or after today for events, tasks, and weather, or the latest occurrence before today for logged calls and historical rates.
